draft.title: Employment contracts
card: Common law contract
an agreement between one employer and one employee. It can be written or spoken, and it sets that person's pay and conditions.
Modern award
a set of minimum pay and conditions for a whole industry or occupation, such as retail. It applies to many employers and employees.
Enterprise agreement
an agreement made at one workplace between the employer and its employees. It must leave employees better off overall than the award.
The National Employment Standards (NES) are ten minimum entitlements, such as annual leave. They apply to all employees covered by the national system, and no contract can go below them.
draft.remember: Contracts and awards set pay and conditions, and none can go below the NES.

a.q: Which agreement is made at a single workplace between that employer and its employees?
opts: An enterprise agreement
A modern award
A common law contract
The National Employment Standards
a.why: An enterprise agreement is made at one workplace and covers the employees there. A modern award covers a whole industry or occupation. A common law contract is tempting, but it is between the employer and one employee, not the group.
a.clue: Think of an agreement for one business and its staff as a group.

b.q: Jo's written contract offers 12 days less annual leave than the National Employment Standards give. What is the effect on Jo's leave?
opts: The NES entitlement applies, as it is the minimum
The contract applies, because Jo signed it
The two amounts are averaged to find Jo's leave
The award for the industry applies in place of the NES
b.why: The NES set a minimum that no contract can go below, so the lower term has no effect and Jo gets the NES entitlement. Signing the contract does not remove the minimum, which is why the second option is wrong.
b.clue: Can a signed contract take away a minimum for all employees?

b.best: The NES entitlement applies, as it is the minimum

problems.detail: The NES now have eleven minimum entitlements, not ten. Casual conversion was added in 2021, so 'ten' is out of date.

An enterprise agreement is not limited to 'one workplace'. A single-enterprise agreement can cover several sites of one employer, and multi-enterprise agreements also exist. 'Made between an employer (or employers) and its employees' would be accurate.

The why says the second option is wrong because signing does not remove the minimum. Options are shown in random order, and in this order the second option is the correct NES answer, so the why contradicts the right answer. It should name the option ('The contract applies, because Jo signed it') rather than its position.
